title: Older man abused by his wife (synthetic)
setting: A social worker visits Harold Pryce, 76, at home at 31 Bramley Road, Harbridge, after his GP raised concerns about bruising, while his wife Sandra is out at the shops.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Mr Pryce? Hello, I'm Tom Okafor, I'm a social worker from Harbridge adult services. Dr Bell asked me to pop round.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh yes, she said someone would come. Come in, mind the step. Call me Harold.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thanks Harold. Lovely garden out the front.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It was. I can't keep on top of it now, with my knees.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I bet. Shall we sit here? So, Dr Bell was a bit worried about you, and she asked me to have a chat about how things are at home. Is now a good time?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Sandra's at the shops, she'll be an hour. So yes.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. I'll be writing notes. What you tell me is confidential, but if I think you're at risk of harm I may need to share it with others, like your GP or the police, and I'd talk to you about that first. Is that alright?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I suppose so.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Let's start with day to day. How are you managing around the house?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Slowly. I've got a stick and a frame upstairs. I had a fall in the garden in the spring.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Any falls since?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, touch wood.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And washing, dressing?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I can wash myself, I sit on a stool in the shower. Socks are the trouble.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, an occupational therapist might help with that. Meals?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Sandra cooks. I can do a sandwich.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And how long have you and Sandra been married?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Nine years. She's my second wife. My first, Joan, died in 2013.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'm sorry. Do you have family nearby?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: My daughter Carol, she's in Kestwick. About two hours away. She rings on Sundays.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Dr Bell mentioned bruises on your arms. Can you tell me how you got those?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Oh. Well. I bruise easily, with the tablets.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That can happen. Is that how these ones happened?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Well. I, er. I don't really like to say.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Take your time, Harold.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Sandra, she, um, she hits me. With her walking stick. When she gets cross.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Thank you for telling me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, no, forget it, I'm making a fuss. Forget I said it. She's not well herself, she gets in pain.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: It's alright. I'm not here to get anyone in trouble, I just want to understand. Can I ask about the bruises on your arms again?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Well. Yes, it's true. She does hit me with the stick, on my arms. I put my arms up, you see.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How often does that happen?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Once a week maybe. More if she's had a bad day.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Is there anything else that happens when she's cross?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Um. Sometimes she, er.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Go on.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: She locks me in the bedroom. When she goes out. She says it's so I don't fall.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How often does she lock you in?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Two or three times a week. For the afternoon. There's no toilet up there.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That must be really difficult. What about your medication, who looks after that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: She does. She keeps them in her handbag.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Do you get them every day?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Not always. If I've annoyed her she keeps my tablets back. Last week I didn't have my heart tablets for three days.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Your heart tablets, for three days. Has that happened before?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: A few times. And my water tablets.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you, Harold. That's really important. Have you thought about whether you want to stay living here?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's my house. Joan and I bought it in 1971. But if I left, she'd take the house. She's always saying that.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Whose name is the house in?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Mine. Just mine. But she says she'd get it, if I went.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. What would you like to happen?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't want her in trouble. I just want it to stop. And I want my tablets.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's really clear. How do you feel about Carol knowing?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Carol never liked her. Yes, you can tell Carol. She'll be upset.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And money, do you manage your own pension?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It goes into a joint account. Sandra does the bills. I've got my own savings book at the post office.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Do you feel safe here tonight?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Tonight, yes. She's going to her sister's tomorrow.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Alright. Here's what I'd suggest. First, I'm going to raise a safeguarding concern with our team, which means we'll look into this properly. Are you happy with that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yes. I think so.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Second, I'll ask Dr Bell today to arrange for your tablets to come from the chemist in a blister pack, delivered to you, so you hold them.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: That'd be good.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Third, I'll ring Carol this week, by Friday, with your permission. And I'll refer you to an occupational therapist for the socks and the stairs.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll also give you the number for the older people's advocacy service, and if you're ever hurt or locked in, ring nine nine nine. Can you reach a phone in the bedroom?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I've got my mobile. Carol made me get one.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Keep it on you. I'll come back on Tuesday the first of December, in the morning, when Sandra's at her sister's. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yes. Thank you, Tom. I'm sorry for all the fuss.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You've nothing to be sorry for, Harold. You did the right thing.

disclosures.what: Harold says his wife Sandra hits him on the arms with her walking stick, about once a week; he takes it back, then says it again.
Harold says Sandra locks him in the bedroom when she goes out, two or three times a week.
must_keep: two or three times a week

disclosures.what: Harold says Sandra keeps his tablets back when he has annoyed her; last week he went without his heart tablets for three days.

controls.must_not_claim: Harold's wife Sandra has taken his house.
